full_judgment:
2. The short facts necessary for the disposal of the appeal may be stated as follows Appellant Abdur Rahman is an Advocate practicing at Chapai-Nawabganj. P.W. 1 Tarikul Islam obtained a decree for delivery of possession in O.C. Suit No. 237 of 1965 in the Court of Munsif Nawabganj. The Appellant Abdur Rahman who is also a surveyor of Nawabganj was appointed by the learned Munsif, Pleader Commissioner for delivery of possession to the decree holder who had deposited the necessary commission fee. The Commissioner executed the writ, but the learned. Munsif on hearing parties concerned directed the decree holder to make a fresh deposit of Rs. 30/- for the Commissioner to go to the locality and verify the measurement of the land. The decree-holder filed a petition with a prayer for giving delivery of possession by removing-structures and enclosures erected on the decretal land by the judgment debtor. Being satisfied that there was mistake committed by the Pleader Commissioner in giving delivery of possession the learned Munsif directed the appellant for giving delivery of possession to the decree-holder in terms of the decree after removing the structure etc. from the decretal land and a report was required to be submitted by the order. This order was passed by the learned Munsif on 18-12-67. 

 3. P.W. 1 sent his son Khairul Islam, P.W. 8 to  know from the learned Pleader Commissioner at his Nawabganj residence as to the date on which he would come The appellant asked P.W.8 to inform his father to come and give him Rs. 50/- and on receipt of that he would go to execute the commission. After this P.W. 1 himself went and met the appellant who demanded Rs. 50/- as illegal gratification from him for doing the work P.W. I told the appellant that he would give the money on Tuesday. Thereafter P.W. 1 and his son P.W. 8 got in touch with Assistant Inspector of District Anti-Corruption Bureau. Mr. Mobarak. Ali, P.W. 9 who wrote out the first information report Ext.1 on the dictation of P.W. 1. He met the Sub-Divisional Officer-in-Charge and obtained his signature on 5, 10 currency notes and arranged for a trap and a first Class Magistrate P.W. 6 was deputed by the Sub-Divisional Officer in charge to witness the trap. P.W. 1 went to the tea stall of P.W. 4 Abdul Bari in the Court compound and met the. appellant there. The appellant demanded the bribe money of Rs. 50/- inside the said Tea stall and P.W.1 paid the same in five 10 rupee signed currency notes which were put in the left pocket of his jacket by the appellant. On getting signal from P.W.s 7 and 8 who had been deputed earlier for this purpose the Magistrate and the Sub-Divisional Public Relation Officer followed by P.W. 9 went inside the lea stall and challenged the appellant who had produced the bribe money from his pocket. The bribe money and the jacket were sieged under seizure list Exhibit 2." Subsequent to this, P.W.9 went to Nawabganj Police Station and filed the complaint exhibits which was treated as first information report. The appellant at the instance of the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor has been charged  with the commission of offence punishable under section 161 of the Penal Code and under section 5(2) of Act 11 of 1947. 

 5. P.W. 1 Tarikul Islam has in his deposition stated that the appellant went to the locality on 9-6-67 and measured the land and was told by the appellant that he would be getting 26 decimals of land. A report was submitted to the court to which an objection was tiled by P.W. 1 and after bearing of the objection the learned Munsif directed the appellant to go to the locality again and to make verification to avoid any mistake. A sum of Rs.50/- was deposited by P.W. 1 on the direction of the court. The appellant was directed by the court to deliver possession to P.W. 1 without any further commission fee. Further he sent his son Khairul Islam P.W.8 to meet the appellant for ascertaining the date of 'his arrival to execute the commission. P.W. 8 informed P.W. 1 after contacting the appellant that the appellant would come on the following Friday in February 1968 and that P.W. 1 should go personally earlier and pay the commissioner Rs. 50/- as asked for by the appellant. Thereafter P.W. 1 met the appellant who demanded Rs. 50/- and said that he would go to the locality on Friday if that amount is paid P.W.1 told him that he would give him the money on Tuesday. Thereafter P.W.1 came to Rajshahi and. Wormed the Anti-Corruption Officer who referred him to the Nawabganj Anti-corruption Daroga. He filed written objection exhibit-1 which was at his instance written by P.W. 9 and he put his signature thereon. Be was then taken to, the S.D.O. but the S.D.O. was absent. The 2nd officer called him in his chamber and he put his signature on 5(five) 10 rupee notes. The signed currency notes were then returned to him. He then went to the Hotel in the court compound where he met the appellant and there on his insistence and demand P.W. 1 took out 5 signed rotes from his pocket and gave then to the appellant who put those notes in the left pocket of his jacket. P.W. 1 and his son Khairul Islam saw this and went away the Diroga, the Magistrate and the publicity officer came. Daroga asked the Advocate whether he had taken the illegal gratification. The appellant denied and told him that he had his own money with him. On the demand of P.W. 9 the appellant look out the said signed notes and gave them in the hand of the Magistrate and notes were then seized. The appellant was thereafter taken to the Nawabgonj Police Station where his jacket was also seized. 

 6. In cross-examination this witness has said that after his petition, if at any time he was called in the chamber of the Munsif he went otherwise not. He submitted petition alleging that the staff had committed for series in his decree but he was not aware if any report to the District Judge was given against him. He came to the District Anti-corruption Officer one day earlier towards the end of January but he did not find him. So he came again and met him on 1-2-68. He did not bring money when he came to Rajshahi to meet the Officer concerned. The Officer concerned did not ask him to go to him with the money or that a trap would be &iced or that on the day he came he was directed by, Head Clerk to go to Nawabganj Anti-corruption Officer. He met the Anti-corruption Daroga on 13-2-68. He has denied that she did not mention it in first information report that his son was sent by him to The appellant and that the appellant had asked his son to tell him to pay Rs. 50/- to the appellant. He met the appellant 2/3 days but he did not remember the subsequent date after being told his son about the date. He met and told him that he would give him Rs. 50/- . This conversation took place at about 4 or 5 P.M. in the compound of the appellant house. Some 10/12 days later on 13-2-68 he gave the appellant the money. In the morning of that day he came to Nawabganj to meet the Daroga, At about 12 mid-day or 1 P.M. he paid the money to the appellant. He came along with P.W. 9 to Nawabganj court where they met the Magistrate between 11 to 12 A.M. in the morning. He and his son were sitting in the court compound from 9 A.M. in front of the Chamber or the  Magistrate. He was given the signed, notes and he from there went to the Tea Stall which is 100/200 cubits from the Magistrate office. He covered the distance by Rickshaw as he is lame and can not walk. He went and sat opposite to the appellant. There was a table between them. About ½ hours lapsed between the signing of the notes by the Magistrate and his giving it to the appellant. There were 5/6 persons at that time in the said Tea Stall. He denied the defence suggestion that he was sitting with the appellant side by side or that he planted the money in the appellant's pocket without his knowledge. He took Tea and sweets with the appellant after the money was paid and then the Daroga and others came. He denied other suggestions of the defence. 

 7. P.W. 2 Asaduzzaman Molla in his evidence said that at about 12 A.M. or 1 P.M. on 13-2-68 the occurrence took place inside a Hotel within the Nawabganj Court compound. He went there to drink water. At that time he saw the appellant  catering inside the said Hotel followed by P. W. 1. The appellant at on a chair and P.W.1 sat on another Chair facing each other. The appellant said, "where is the money? where upon the P.W. 1 took out 10 rupee notes and gave to the appellant who put the same with his left hand in his own left ticket packet. I hereafter the appellant and P.W.1 started taking tea. There A.I.D A.B. and third Officer came in to the Hotel. The third Officer sat on a Chair to the right of the appellant in another table and the I.O. confronted the appellant and stated that he would search him. Many people came and he could not sec who brought out the money but he saw that five 10 rupee currency notes were being counted by the third officer. He is a seizure witness and he signed the seizure list exhibit-2. In cross-examination he stated that he was a man of Mohadanga which is 2 miles from Nawabganj Court. He is a cultivator by profession. He had no case in Court but had gone inside the hotel and sat there, and only 1 or 2 minutes later the appellant followed by P.W.1 entered. He was in the hotel for about 20 minutes and he saw the occurrence. He did not see P.W.8 sitting on a chair. He could not remember to have told the investigation Officer that small son of Tarikul was sitting and he got up on seeing the payment, when he came to the hotel. There was another customer eating rice. Then he saw the appellant and P.W.1 entering. He said that he did not tell the investigating Officer about taking tea and not water in the hotel. At first the money was paid to the appellant and then P.W. 1 took tea. He did not see any sweets on the table. He has denied the defence sugestions. 

 8 P.W.3 Jahur Ali Biswas was member of the Shahabazpur Union Council. His evidence is to the effect that on the date of occurrence which is about the middle of February 1968 and the time would be 11/12 A. M. or near about that time. He went to the Hotel to take his meal. He saw the appellant sitting on the Chair beside a table and P.W.1 was also sitting on a chair by the side of the same table and then he saw the third officer of Nawabganj, the A.I.D.B. and the publicity Officer and few others entered the hotel and the publicity officer and the Magistrate sat on 2 chairs and the A.I.D.A.B. went to the table of the appellant and stated to the appellant that he had taken money. On that the appellant replied that he had no bribe money in his possession. The people assembled there saw five 10 rupee currency notes in the table of the appellant. The Magistrate and other people were also near the table at that time. He did not himself sec who brought out the money. A seizure list was prepared and he signed the same. In cross-examination this witness said that before the entry of the Magistrate he saw the appellant and P.W.1 in the hotel who were taking food on the same table. The appellant and P.W.1 were a little &stance from him. He could not remember whether they were sitting side by side or face to face. He has denied the defence suggestion P.W. 4. A. Bari is the hotel owner where the occurrence took place. He was in the kitchen at the relevant time. He did not know the appellant and P.W. 1 from before. When he came out from the kitchen he saw the Magistrate party there. Then he saw the appellant trying to take out the hand-kerchief but the Daroga caught hold of his hand and said that he had received bribe from Tarique. He then busied himself in providing chairs near the table of Magistrate and was worried over the whole thing. He did not, however, see who brought out the money but saw five 10 rupee currency notes on the table on which P.W.3 was taking his meals. In cross-examination he said that he could not remember which hand of the accused had been caught by the I.O. at the time when the appellant was about to take out his handkerchief P.W. 5 Mohsin Ali is a surveyor under the circle officer (Dev.). There is nothing in his evidence regarding the occurrence. P.W. 6 Md. Yunus was the Magistrate 1st Class on the date of occurrence he was deputed by the S.D.O. to witness the trap of the appellant and he witnessed the same. P.W. 9 and some other person whom he did not remember were with him at the time of the trap which was within the Nawabganj Civil Court compound. He did not know the appellant from before P.W. 9 recovered the money from the appellant who took out and handed over the five I.O. rupee currency notes and compared the number of the currency notes with the number which were given to him by the S.D.O. in charge. He saw the signatures of S.D.O. in charge. He seized the currency notes. At the time of the seizure of the currency notes he put his initial on each of those notes. P.W. 10 was also with him at that time and he also put his signature on the notes. Seizure exhibit-2 was prepared by P.W. 9 and he attested the seizure list. In cross-examination he has said that a written order deputing him was produced in his chamber. He went to the tea stall from his chamber with P.W. The appellant was present inside the tea stall and there was another man in front of him. When he entered into the tea stall the appellant was eating but he could not remember if the appellant was taking tea or sweet. He could not remember if the told the I. O. that the appellant was thing tea. He went first along with P.W. 10 and sat inside the tea stall. Thereafter P.W. 9 entered and challenged the appellant by saying that In had bribe money with him. The appellant told him that he had taken money for performing his work and he took out the money from the pocket. P.W. 9 seized the money and arrested the appellant. This witness could not remember if he told the I.O. that the appellant had said that he had accepted money for (performing work). He did not tell the I.O. that the appellant first denied having received money. When the appellant produced the money from his pocket, the money was seized by the I.O.. He did not state to the I.O. that they and I.O. went together and on their arrival P.W. 9 challenged the appellant. He has denied the defence suggestion. 

 P.W. 7 Abdus Samad constable who was standing at a distance of about 8/9 yds was told by P.W. 9 that P.W. 8, son of P.W. 1 would signal him after the payment of money by P.W.I and he in his turn would signal P.W. 9 on getting the signal from P.W. 8 from outside the door of the tea stall. He signaled P.W.9 who then took the Magistrate with him and went to the tea stall. In cross-examination he had said that he stood in front of the tea stall for about 5/10 minutes. He signaled P. W. 9 who was 25 yds away. The Magistrate went first inside the tea stall along with 1/2 other and then P. W. 9 went inside the tea stall. He could not remember if he did not tell the I.O. regarding this signal or that P. W. 9 would signal to him. He denied various defence suggestions. P. W. 8 is the son of P. W. 1 has corroborated P. W. 1 regarding the story of the giving of money, regarding going to Rajshahi and Nawabganj. He has also corroborated his father regarding the manner they went to the tea stall on the instruction of P. W. 9 he stood in front of the out side door of the tea stall. The appellant demanded and his father gave Rs. 50/. Then he signaled the police. The Magistrate and the Publicity Officer and P. W. 9 entered the hotel. He had seen another man taking meal inside the hotel. In cross-examination he has said that he visited the house of appellant 6 months earlier. He went and met the appellant for getting date about 3 or 4 P.M. He has denied to have told P. W. 9 that the appellant had said about his going on Friday next. Their village house is 7 miles away from Nawabganj court. He has further stated in cross-examination about the going to Rajshahi twice, he told about the going to Nawabganj on the following day of their arrival at Nawabganj the trap was managed. They stayed in Siddique hotel on the day previous to the trap. He denied the suggestion that he was not moving with his father at Nawabganj. They met the 2nd Officer in Court at about 9/10 A.M. About 12 A.M. or 1 P.M. he and his father went to the hotel. He remained outside the hotel. He denied to have told the P. W. 9 that he and his father sat in the hotel and then the appellant came and began to take sweets with his father. He saw the Magistrate and P. W. 9 after he gave signal. He did not see them before the signal at that time. The money was paid to the appellant for whom he worked from before. The appellant took out the money and gave it to P. W. 9 and not to the Magistrate. The Magistrate sat on a Chair one Chair intervening from that of the appellant. He denied to have told P. W. 9 that Magistrate asked the appellant to bring out the money and the appellant brought out the same and handed it to the Magistrate. He denied the defence suggestions of the painting. 

 9 P. W. 9 Md. Mobarak Ali who the Assistant Inspector of District Anti-Corruption Bureau, Dinajpur said in his deposition that on 13.2.68 he was approached by one Tariqul Islam (P. W. 1) in his office at Nawabganj and he recorded the complaint of P. W. 1 and arranged for a trap. P. W. 1 produced before him five 10 rupee currency notes. He made written prayer to the Sub-Divisional Officer. He placed the written prayer and the currency notes before the S. D. O. in charge and passed the order deputing P. W. 6 to accompany him to witness the trap. At about 1 P.M. the trap was arranged and on getting signal he, P. W. 6 and P. W. 10 went to the tea stall of P. W. 4 and he found the appellant and P. W. 1 sitting face to face. P. W. 1 told him that the appellant had taken bribe of Rs. 50/-. He challenged the appellant. He produced the money and the appellant brought out the money from the left pocket of his jacket and admitted that the money was given to him by P. W. 1. The currency notes were compared by P. W. 6 and P. W. 10. He seized the notes and prepared the seizure list exhibit-2 and then went to the Nawabganj Police Station where he filed the P. W. 1's complaint with his endorsement for being treated as F. I. R. In cross-examination he has said that he did not know P. W. 1 from before and he met him at about 9 A.M. on the date of occurrence. He recorded the statement exhibit-1 as narrated by P. W. 1. At about 12 A. M. He met the S. D. O. in charge in his chamber. Thereafter he went to P. W. 6. The currency notes were signed and returned to P. W, 1. He instructed the F. W. 1 to pay notes to the appellant if they are demanded by the appellant. He denied various defence suggestions that he directed P. W. 1 to put the money in the pocket of the appellant somehow or other. P. W. 1 had told him earlier that money will be received by the appellant in tea stall. They went after getting signal. The Magistrate went first and then he went behind him. He went in after being told by P. W. 1. He challenged the appellant who stated that P. W. 1 had given Rs. 50/- and he brought out the same. He denied the difference suggestions that the appellant had stated that he had not taken any bribe money. 

 10 P.W. 10 A.K. S. Nur Mohammad was the Sub-Divisional Public Relation Officer at Nawabganj at relevant time. He has said that on the date of occurrence he had accompanied the third officer at the tea stall and he saw P. W. 1 in the tea stall and also the appellant sitting face to face. P. W. 6 asked the appellant to bring out money but the appellant was unwilling first but then he took out five 10 rupee currency notes from the left pocket of his jacket and gave it to P. W. 6 and they were seized and they signed the same. In cross-examination he said that he was going home which is about a mile away from the court and then he and the Magistrate went straight to the tea stall but could not say whether P. W. 1 and appellant were taking tea or not. He had denied the defence suggestions that he went to the tea stall after the whole thing was over. 

 11 P.W. 13 Md. Nazar Ali was the Assistant Inspector of District Anti Corruption Bureau Rajshahi who took over the charge of investigation of the case from P. W. 9. He seized some records from the Munsif court and examined two witnesses. In cross-examination be has said that he received a copy of the first information report and took up the investigation from 29.2.68. He has further stated that P. W. 1 told him that he met Bara Shaheb at Rajshahi who told him to fix up date of payment of money and then to come to him and he will make all arrangement and that after fixing the date as 13.2.68 he came to Rajshahi, but not finding Bara Shahab he met his Head clerk. P. W. 1 did not tell him that he sent his son to the appellant or that appellant asked his son to send his father with Rs. 50/- or that P. W. 1 met the appellant and the P. W. 1 was asked to come with money on Friday but P. W. 1 said that he would bring money on Tuesday. P. W. 1 also did not tell him that his son left after seeing the giving of money. P. W. 2 told him that one young son of Tariqul was sitting in the hotel and got up and left. P. W. 2 told him that he was taking tea at that time P. W. 3 did not tell him that he heard from the Investigating Officer and Magistrate that the money had been found in the pocket of the appellant P. W. 6 told him that P. W. 1 and the appellant were sitting side by side and at first the appellant denied the payment of money. P. W. 6 did not tell him that the appellant had admitted taking of the money (for performing his work) P. W. 7 did not till him that Tariqul Islam signaled him P. W. 8 did not tell him that the appellant would go for completion of work on Friday. P. W. 8 told him that after one day his father along went and met the appellant at Nawabganj P. W. 8 did not tell him that after he and his father went inside the hotel the appellant came on seeing them P. W. 8 quickly went and informed P. W. 7. He did not speak about signal P. W. 8 told him that the Magistrate asked the appellant to bring out the money and the appellant brought out and gave, it in the hand of the Magistrate. He stated that there were not many people in the hotel at the time of giving money. 

 12 D. W. 1 Ranjit Kumar Bagchi is an advocate of Nawabganj and has said in his evidence that his father is also an Advocate. He does the work of his father's Sherista. They represented the P. W. 1 in the Court. The appellant was appointed commissioner in the case and gave notice on 3. 2.68 fixing the commission date on 16.2.68 and the respective lawyers of the parties were notified. He proved notice exhibit-B signed by the appellant and he also proved his father's signature and also the signature of the lawyer for the judgment debtor. In cross-examination he has said that two days after the receipt of the notice dated 3.2.68, they informed the decree holder by post card. 

 13. It is clear from the case as brought out by the prosecution that P. W. 1 had been moving with the officers of the Anti-corruption Department at Rajshahi and Nawabganj for about 2 weeks before the date of occurrence. According to P.W. 1 he came to Rajshahi but could not met the officer of the Anti-corruption Department towards the end of January and he went again to Rajshahi, on 1.2.68. Thereafter he met P.W. 9 at Nawabganj on 11.2.68. The reason for this was that the appellant had asked for Rs. 50/- to be paid to him before he went to do the commission work as directed by the learned Munsif. The learned Munsif it may be recalled has passed. The order on 28.11.67 and required that the report be submitted by 28.12. 67. P. W. 1 had sent his son to the appellant for ascertaining the date of his visit to the locality for the commission. The appellant told P. W. 8 to inform P. W. 1 to come to see him with Rs. 50, P. W. 1 thereupon met the appellant and agreed to pay Rs. 50/- on Tuesday. It is to be noticed that the prosecution has not made any attempt to specify the date on which this arrangement was arrived at between the appellant and P. W. 1. The prosecution has left sufficient gap by rising the phrases such as towards the end of January, Tuesday following Friday. 

 The story as given by P. W. 1 regarding the payment of money has been sought to be corroborated by P. W. 8, the son of P. W. 1. In the cross-examination of P. W. 8 it is found that he and his father came to Nawabganj of the day previous to the day of occurrence i.e. 12. 2. 68. P. W. 1 does not mention this in his evidence at all. There is also no mention in the evidence of either P. W. 1 or P. W. 8 that the payment was to be made in public place such as in a tea stall. It is only P. W. 9 who says that P. W. 1 told him that the money was arranged to be paid in the Tea Stall. Without specifying in which tea stall the said payment was to be made. The prosecution also laid no evidence to show that this was the only tea stall. This arrangement with the Anti-corruption Department and the demand of money by the appellant from P. W. 1 and P. W. 8 as has been mentioned there is no particular date there. The non-mentioning of specified date about going to Rajshahi. Anti-corruption Department and then after a lapse of 8 or 10 days going to Nawabganj. Anti-Corruption Department assure some importance because of the evidence of D.W.1 and exhibit-B the notice given by the Appellant Commissioner to D. W. 1. 

 14 The learned whole time Special Judge missed the importance of this aspect of the case. The defence has proved that on 3.2.68 notice was given by the appellant to the parties concerned fixing 16.2.68 as the commission date. The prosecution's failure to giver specified dates of the demand of money by the appellant and P. W. 1's going over to Rajshahi and Nawabganj create cloud in the prosecution case. Apart from this, if the occurrence itself is tested it is to be seen that according to P. W. 1 he came to tea stall by a rickshaw and found the appellant sitting inside the tea stall. P.W. 2 has said in his examination in chief that he saw the appellant entering this hotel followed by P. W. 1 and P. W. 8 who, is the only other witness to this has said that the appellant commissioner had  uttered into the tea stall earlier than his father who went by a Rickshaw from the S. D. O. court building. On this point there is contradiction in the evidence of P. W. 1, P. W . 2 and P. W. 8 regarding the payment of money and recovery. P. W. 1. in his evidence has said that on the insistence and demand of the appellant he took from his pocket the five signed notes and gave those to the appellant who put them in his pocket and then the "Daroga and the 3rd Officer (Magistrate) and the Publicity Officer came and the Daroga asked the appellant whether he had taken illegal gratification. The accused denied and said that he had his own money with him. On the demand or "Daroga" to take out his "own money" the accused took out the said Signed notes and gave them in the hand of the 3rd Officer (Magistrate) and the notes were seized then and there. P. W. 2 aid, "The accused said; "where is the money where upon the P. W. 1 took on 10 rupee notes and gave to the accused who put the same with his left hand in his own left at pocket. Then the P. W. 1 and the accused started taking tea. Then I saw the A.I.O.A.B. and the third officer coming to the hotel. The Third Officer sat on a chair towards right of the accused in another table, and the I.O. confronted the accused and stated that he will search him. Then many people came and could not see who brought out the money but I saw that five 10 rupee notes were being counted by the 3rd Officer. 

 P.W. 3 has said "Then I saw that the 3rd officer (Magistrate) of Nawabganj, the A.I.D.A.B. and the publicity officer a few others entered the hotel and the Magistrate and publicity officer sat on 2 chairs and the A.I.D.A.B. went to the table of the accused and stated to the accused that he (latter) had taken, money and the accused replied that he had no bribe money in his possession. Then 10/20 people assembled. Then I saw five 10 rupee notes on the table in front of the accused. The Magistrate and other people were near that table at that time. P. W. 4 has said on this point, when I came out of my kitchen, I saw the A.I.D.A.B. near the accused Abdur Rahman whom I saw but do not remember if the P. W. 1 was sitting or standing. Then I saw the accused standing and trying to take out his handkerchief from pocket of his pant, but the Daroga caught hold of his hand and said that he had received bribe from Tarique. Then I busied myself in providing chairs near the table to the Magistrate and others and I myself worried. I did not see who brought out the money, but then I saw five 10 rupee currency notes on the table on which P. W. Zohur Ali had taken his meal and there the Daroga was also standing, and Magistrate and other sat nearly. "It is to be noted that the incident of taking out the handkerchief and catching hold of the hand of appellant, is not to be seen in the evidence of any other witness. 

 15. P. W. 6 on this point has said, "I do not know the accused from before. The A.I.D.A.B. Mobarak Ali recovered the money from the accused who took out and handed over the 5 ten rupee notes compared the numbers of the currency notes as the numbers were given to me by the S. D. O. in charge. "In cross-examination he said, "I went first along with the S.D.P.R.O. and sat inside the tea stall and soon there after the A.I.D.A.B, entered, and challenged the accused by saying that he had bribe money with him. The accused said that he had taken money for performing his work, and then he took out the money from his pocket. "It is to be seen from the evidence of this witness that this part of his statement regarding the taking of money for performing his work, has not been corroborated by any witness and the Investigating Officer P. W. 13 has in his evidence said that in his statement under section 161 of the code this witness did not speak about taking the money for performing work. P. W. 8 has said on this point. "The accused commissioner demanded and my father gave Rs. 50/-Then I gave signal to the police. Thereafter I saw the Magistrate and the publicity officer and the I. O. enter the hotel. I had seen one other man eating inside the hotel," this witness in his examination in chief has not said anything about the recovery of the money.In cross-examination he has said, "the accused took out the money and gave to the A.I.D.A.B", and not to the Magistrate. The Magistrate sat on a chair one chair intervening from that of the accused." P. W. 9 has said on this point," Tariqul Islam stated that accused had taken bribe of Rs. 50/00 and I challenged the accused to produce the money and bring it out. Then he (accused) brought out the money from his left side pocket of his coat, and admitted that the money was given to him by P. W. 1. "The admission so made as stated by this witness is not corroborated by other witness. P. W. 10 has said on this point "The third Officer Mr. Yunus asked the accused to bring out bribe money but the accused was unwilling first but he took out five 10 rupee notes from left pocket of his coat and made it over to the Magistrate." When the 3rd Officer told the accused that he (accused) had taken bribe money, the accused denied." The statement of this witness regarding the Magistrate's asking the appellant to bring out the bribe money and making over the same to the Magistrate P.  21. This point of view which I am unable to express in any better than that has been expressed in the case of M. C. Mitra Vs. the State reported in A.I.R. 1951 Cal. 524. Their Lordships observed as follows :— 

 "Before I conclude I wish to express this Court's great disapprobation of the practice that seems to have become very frequent of sending Magistrate as witnesses of police trap. The Magistrate is made to go under disguise to witness the trap laid by the police. In this case it was Presidency Magistrates and in other cases which have come to our notice there have been other Magistrate who became such witnesses. To make the Magistrate a party or limb of the police during the police investigation seriously and entrains the independence of the Magistrates and perverts, their judicial outlook. The Magistrates are the normal custodians of the general administration of criminal justice and it is they who normally decide and pass judgments on the acts and conducts of the police. It is not enough to say, therefore that the Magistrate acting as a witness in a particular case does not himself try that case. This practice is all the more indefensible here specially when there is no separation of the executive from the judiciary. The basic merit of administration of criminal justice in the state lies in the fact that the person arrested by the police is entitled to come before an independent and impartial Magistrate who is expected to deal with the case, without the Magistrate himself being in any way a parties an or a witness to police activities. There is another danger and that is the Magistrate are put in the unenviable and  embarrassing position of having to give evidence as witness and then being disbelieve. That is not the way to secure respect for the Magistracy charged with the administration of justice. In my judgment this practice which is unfair to the accused & unfair to the Magistrate. It is also unfair to the police. Because charged with the high responsibility and duty of performing a great and essential public service of this state the police can not offer to run the risk of opprobrium even if unfounded, that they have enlisted the Magistrate in their cause, that risk is too great & involves for feting public respect and confidence."
